AGENDA

Meetings are broadcast live on Glendale TV, viewable on Spectrum Cable, channel 6, and AT&T U-
verse, channel 99. Meetings are also streamed live in high definition (HD) on the city's webpage,
glendaleca.gov/live (https://www.glendaleca.gov/live),  on  YouTube.com/myglendale
(https://www.YouTube.com/myglendale), and on Apple TV, Roku, and Amazon Fire devices using a
free app called Screenweave and choosing “Glendale TV” from the menu. Meetings are also
archived on the City Website for viewing anytime at glendaleca.gov/agendas
(https://www.glendaleca.gov/agendas). Call (818) 548-4013 for program schedules. DVDs of the
proceedings are available for purchase in the City Clerk's Office. For public comments and
questions during the meeting, call (818) 937-8100. Public comments on a specific agenda item will
be taken when that agenda item is discussed. If you have any question about matters on the
agenda, or requests for assistance, please contact the City Clerk at (818) 548-2090 during regular
business hours.
  PLEASE TURN OFF CELLULAR PHONES WHILE INSIDE THE MEETING LOCATION
In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign
language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon request. Assisted listening devices
are available same-day upon request. At least 48 hours (or two business days) notice is required for
requests regarding sign language translation and Braille transcription services. All documents
related to open session items on this agenda that are received less than 72 hours prior to this
meeting, and are public records, will be available for review in the Office of the City Clerk, 613 E.
Broadway, RM 110, Glendale, CA 91206.
Translation services are provided for meetings through the use of bilingual staff for speakers who
wish to utilize the service as available. Speakers should state their request by contacting the City
Clerk’s office at (818) 548-2090, at least 24 hours prior to the scheduled meeting. Please specify
the language for which you require translation. The exclusive use of City provided interpreters is not
required and persons are welcome to use their own interpreter or speak in their native language.

5. CITY COUNCIL/STAFF COMMENTS
  Councilmember Devine attended the groundbreaking of the Harrower Village housing project
  for seniors. She announced that the Adams Hill Art Festival will be held on August 28th,
  “Touch the Truck” event will be held on September 25th, and Sunrise Rotary’s Community
  Connection Clean-up Service Day event will be held on October 8th. She asked staff to provide
  a report on the revision of the historic district process and the status of the creation of
  brochures outlining the benefits and responsibilities of homeowners in historic districts. City
  Manager Roubik Golanian provided a brief update on this issue. Devine stated there is
  unpermitted work being done in the city by residents. She asked staff to provide
  recommendations to increase the penalties for these violations and prioritize these
  complaints. Brotman seconded.

  Councilmember Brotman asked staff to look into having an annual or bi-annual event called
  “Bring your E-Waste” day, wherein resident bring their electronics to properly dispose them for
  free. He also asked staff to look into setting up a “fix-it” clinic or “repair café,” where residents
  bring in their small appliances to have them fixed instead of disposing them. Golanian
  indicated that Sustainability Officer David Jones will provide a report on this issue.

  Councilmember Najarian announced that Metro is constructing a transit line that will connect
  Glendale directly to LAX terminals. He was absent from last Tuesday’s meeting because he
  was at the Dodger stadium throwing the first pitch. Najarian represented the City of Glendale
  and Metro Board at the game and promoted the Dodger Stadium Express, which is a free ride

  3
   from Union Station to the Dodger stadium. Earlier that day, he met with the Federal Railroad
  Administrator from Washington DC and they talked about safety detection and increase in
  funding for services along the railroad corridor of the San Fernando Road from Union Station
  all the way to the Hollywood Burbank Airport. Najarian asked staff to look into the unpermitted
  work and violations caused by G Lounge Bar. City Manager Roubik Golanian provided a brief
  update.

  Councilmember Asatryan attended the Independent Cities Conference this weekend where
  clean energy, public safety, water issues, and Senate Bill 9 were discussed. She asked staff
  to look into what the City of Lancaster is doing in terms of clean energy. Golanian stated that
  he will speak to the City Manager of Lancaster to see if there are any opportunities for
  collaboration and any best practices that we can learn from. Asatryan indicated that she
  supports Devine’s motion on unpermitted work. She spoke about the warehouse explosion
  that took place in Yerevan, Armenia where many people were injured and some lost their
  lives. Asatryan also addressed the war crimes committed by the Azerbaijani military in
  Artsakh. She asked council to adjourn in memories of the victims and asked to keep the
  people of Armenia and Artsakh in our thoughts.

  Mayor Kassakhian had reached out to the Deputy Consulate General of Armenia in Los
  Angeles and had expressed his condolences and asked to convey our collective condolences
  to the Mayor of the City of Yerevan. Kassakhian stated that the Concert in the Park series has
  ended and he looks forward to next year’s events. He stated that classes have resumed and
  asked the public to drive safely and wished students a successful academic year. Mayor
  Kassakhian thanked Housing Authority Chair Brotman for his comments at the
  groundbreaking of the Harrower Village senior housing project. He indicated that it was a well-
  attended event and stated that it is very exciting to see the work that the city is doing about
  affordable housing regardless of what was erroneously written in an LA Times article.
  Kassakhian attended the Miss Philippines USA pageant and was impressed to see young
  women take pride in their culture and heritage. He asked to adjourn the council meeting in
  memory of Shirak Khojayan.
